title: MT82 manual transmission specifications
introduction:
I identify the transmission and engine application before using this reference. The materials table pairs products with their specifications; the capacity and general-specification tables cover fluid quantity, weight and input-shaft rotational resistance. For gear ratios, choose the fitted engine’s column before reading across from the gear—sharing a gearbox name does not make every application’s gearing identical.

These are reference specifications. Material application points, additive quantity, filling and level checks, handling, and rotational-torque measurement setup belong to the matching service procedure.

edits.text: Specified lubricants, fluids, sealers and adhesives
edits.why: Read each product name alongside its part number and material specification. I treat this as a materials catalog, not a cocktail recipe: the presence of several fluids and greases does not mean they share an application point.

edits.text: Footnote a: XL-18 is required only after synchronizer replacement.
edits.why: Synchronizers bring rotating transmission parts toward compatible speeds before a gear engages. The footnote makes the additive requirement conditional on their replacement rather than a blanket requirement for every fluid service.
The capacity row expresses the fluid quantity in quarts and liters. Keep the chosen unit attached to the value when planning the fluid supply.

Read the weight in the unit you need. The rotational-torque maximum concerns resistance while turning the input shaft, which receives engine rotation through the clutch. Keep that meaning distinct from a fastener tightening torque.

Choose the column headed with the fitted engine, then read across from the desired gear. Larger numerical ratios provide more torque multiplication; smaller ratios permit more road speed for a given engine speed with the rest of the driveline unchanged. Keep each ratio attached to its engine column.
